assertion_audit.failure_condition: A dry pass reporting itself as an applied one.
The dry arm removing an aged entry.
The applied pass no longer unlinking an entry past the age threshold; the recorded mutation of _expired_persisted_memos reproduces exactly this red.
Inverting or dropping the mtime comparison so an entry inside the window is removed.
Removing a different file, or reporting an unremoved row as removed.
Dropping the announcement, or writing it to a channel the test does not read.
The sweep reaching memo entries through a path other than _persisted_memo_roots.
A pass that reports memo rows it did not derive from the memo roots.

assertion_independence: No input-echo assertion was found: each added assertion compares the filesystem or the pass report against a path the test created before the call, so none holds whatever the code does; the one channel assertion at tests/test_the_persisted_memo_store_has_a_bound.py:72 checks where the announcement went, which is the property under review, not a round-tripped value.

findings.text: blocking: `_expired_persisted_memos` announces each removal with print() to stdout, but both callers emit their report as a JSON document on stdout — reckon/crew/gc.py:2230 is the `python -m reckon.crew.gc --apply` entry the retention service runs, and the crew gc and crew retention-sweep commands emit through _emit — so any applied pass that removes one aged memo leaves stdout that json.loads cannot parse, while the two sibling sweeps in the same file announce on sys.stderr (gc.py:484 ledger caches, gc.py:548 picker views); write the line to sys.stderr and read capsys.readouterr().err at tests/test_the_persisted_memo_store_has_a_bound.py:72.

non-blocking: PERSISTED_MEMO_KINDS enumerates three of the cache kinds written through metadata_index._persisted_cache_path (reckon/metadata_index.py:1863), so route-result (reckon/route_results.py:94), git-creation (reckon/git_dates.py:59), git-last-modified (reckon/git_dates.py:412) and compliance (reckon/compliance.py:139) entries still accumulate with every distinct key, and the store is bounded only for the three swept families.

non-blocking: the sweep wired into the run-less gc pass has no test — tests/test_the_persisted_memo_store_has_a_bound.py drives retention_sweep only — so deleting the garbage_collect call or its run_id-is-None guard leaves the suite green while `crew gc --apply` stops bounding the store.
